newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SOROS SAYS POUND UNLIKELY TO BE IN EMU AT LAUNCH.
newsitem.headline: SOROS SAYS POUND UNLIKELY TO BE IN EMU AT LAUNCH.

text.p: World-famous financier George Soros said on Wednesday he thought it was unlikely the British pound would be ready to join European Monetary Union (EMU) at its launch in January 1999.
"I don't think the British pound will is likely to be included in the EMU at its launch in January, 1999," he told journalists during a brief visit to the Slovak capital.

Soros, head of multi-billion-dollar U.S. investment funds, added that he expected a single European currency to be launched as planned at the beginning 1999, though the Spanish peseta and Italian lira also were not likely to be included in from the start.
"But by that time (the start of EMU), there should be clear conditions under which these currencies will be incorporated in the single European currency very soon after it is launched," Soros said.
Soros declined to comment on how he saw development of U.S. dollar as result of a meeting of the Group of Seven (G7) finance ministers in Berlin last month.
"Since I know exactly what the next development of the (U.S.) dollar will be, I will not answer this question," he said.
Asked whether this meant that he planned to speculate on dollar development, Soros said: "We can all speculate."
The G7 said after the meeting that the sharp fall in the dollar seen in 1995 had been corrected, indicating they wanted the dollar to hold steady at the higher levels reached.
The Hungarian-born financier's speculations are credited with having almost single-handedly driven the British pound out of the Exchange Rate Mechanism in 1992.
During the meeting, Soros repeatedly warned against some financial derivatives, which, he said, threaten the stability on the world financial markets.
"Most of all, I have in mind the so-called knock-out options, which are a real danger for the stability of the world markets," he said.
He added that these instruments should not be banned by administrative measures, but that they should be "very closely watched." "Just like you watch the earthquake warnings."
